item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So, by the nature of the wiki there is no record to consult, but the framing trope (cross-outs from a document-altering smart-alek object) has been tried multiple times as a -J and failed.

This is partially because, as Roget says, 1561 already exists and is very good, and cross-outs make things difficult to read. On top of those, as a source of humor, a basic object trying to make itself sound awesome and calling others stupid is a pretty shallow well.

Not trying to jump down your throat. For a first post, it's generally well written, and those are some very fine ruler puns. Seriously, quite good. Just saying, what you're banking on for whimsy or absurdity comes off instead as a rather tired trope. (Anyone else remember the sexy white sphere?)

-1

In addition, it's really annoying to try and read an article where every other word is crossed out. -1.

Thanks for the responses.

In regards to the above.

+ show block
– hide block

I can see how the strokes would confuse one's reading of the article. It just seemed humorous to show how bad the ruler is at its job. It truly believes it has immense power yet people just shrug it off. I was not sure how else to pull these thoughts into the article. I won't lie, though, I was aiming for pun-ch lines (lel) before the scip even took form.

The final addendum was basically another jab at how useless the ruler is. The Foundation would have been dishing out amnestic showers, or clearing out surrounding areas if this thing caused all stationery in a 10km radius to gravitate towards it. However, it is so easy to just move the stuff that the Foundation has to do shit-all (It's basically: Leave work. Come back next day. Hmm my pencil seems to have rotated 3mm to the right. Shrug. Continue working). Which must hurt our magnificent rulers feels.

/me points and laughs.

If the scip doesn't appeal to some, that's okay. This is my first scip posted, after all.
